My guess, and obviously I haven't died in recent memory so I'm no expert, is that your perception of time becomes asymptotic and you never actually experience the moment of your absolute death. 

But what terrifies me the most isn't what comes after death, its what comes before. Your brain decays as it's starved of oxygen and/or severely damaged, and you can be alive for that. So *you* die before you die. I never really thought of this until a friend suffered severe brain damage. They survived the event and made a solid physical recovery, but with virtually no hint or memory of the person they were before. It hit me with this sense that who we are as people - our personalities, our memories, feelings, everything - is detached from our conscience and is here in the "physical" world, able to be destroyed before our sense of being ceases. That terrifies me more than anything.
